Call recording and consent: a plain-English guide

On this page
One-party and all-party consentHow to tell callersStoring and sharing recordingsUsing recordings wellFinal thoughts

Recording calls is routine, but the rules about telling people vary by place. This guide explains the main ideas in everyday language.

Teams record calls for training, quality and disputes. All of those are good reasons, and all of them depend on doing it with permission.

This is general information, not legal advice. Check the rules where you and your callers are located, or ask a qualified adviser, before you roll out recording.

One-party and all-party consent

Laws generally fall into two groups. In one-party consent places, a person who is on the call may record it. In all-party consent places, everyone on the call must agree.

  • One-party. Only one participant, such as your agent, needs to know about the recording.
  • All-party. Every participant must be told and agree, usually through an announcement.
  • Calls that cross borders. The stricter rule is the safe one to follow.

Many teams follow the strictest rule everywhere, because it is simpler than tracking each caller's location.

How to tell callers

AnnouncePlay a short notice at the start of the call.
ContinueStaying on the line signals agreement where that is allowed.
Offer a choiceGive callers a way to decline where you can.
Log itKeep a record that the notice played.
Tip: keep the notice short and clear

"Calls may be recorded for quality and training" is easy to understand. Long legal paragraphs are skipped.

Storing and sharing recordings

  • Limit access. Only people who need recordings should be able to open them.
  • Set a retention period. Delete recordings after the time you actually need them.
  • Protect sensitive data. Pause recording when payment details are read out.
  • Respond to requests. Be ready to find or delete a recording when someone asks.

Using recordings well

The value is in using what you record: coaching agents, settling disputes and finding patterns.

"We play two short examples at each team meeting. Nobody finds it intrusive because everyone knows why we do it."

Operations director (sample quote)

Final thoughts

Recording is simple to turn on and easy to get wrong. Know which rules apply, tell people clearly, restrict access and delete on schedule. Take a look at call recording and the controls that help.
